blocks.x: The honest pitch for provenance, traceability & supply chain trust fits in a sentence — Proof, not paperwork — EUDR, DPP and chain-of-custody systems regulators and customers can verify. — and the rest of this page is the how: measured baseline, bounded build, evidence in flight.
What we deliver under this name

Provenance is becoming a compliance requirement: EU Deforestation Regulation due diligence, Digital Product Passports, food-safety traceability, conflict-minerals reporting. We build traceability systems that survive audits: capture at source (mobile-first for farmers, scanners for factories), cryptographic anchoring of custody events, identity for participants (including decentralized ID where anonymous intermediaries exist), and verification interfaces for regulators, customers and auditors — each seeing only what their role permits.

The data engineering matters as much as the ledger: sensor and IoT feeds at critical custody points, master-data alignment across participants, and analytic layers for risk scoring (deforestation proximity, contamination windows, authenticity signals). The result is chain-of-custody that answers regulator queries in hours and powers premium positioning — verified provenance is a market, not just a control.

Programs of Provenance, Traceability & Supply Chain Trust run in Agriculture & Food Systems, Retail & Consumer Goods, Manufacturing & Industrial, Logistics & Supply Chain — always against one named number, always with the baseline signed first.
